original.description: A German spiked helmet — Pickelhaube — with its field cover (Feldüberzug) fitted, exhibited in the Braunschweigisches Landesmuseum and dated by the museum to 1914–1916. The cover is the point: the parade helmet went to war under grey cloth, spike and all.
original.date: 18 November 2014 (the photograph); the object is dated 1914–1916 by the museum
original.archive: Braunschweigisches Landesmuseum, Braunschweig (the collection); photograph held on Wikimedia Commons
original.licence: public domain (Commons record: LicenseShortName "Public domain"; UsageTerms "Public domain"; AttributionRequired false — the photographer released the photograph and the object is out of copyright).

colorization.status: not colorized, and must not be — a modern colour photograph of the object.

content_policy: ok — a museum object on display; no casualties
caption: A Pickelhaube under its field cover, Braunschweigisches Landesmuseum, dated 1914–1916. Germany had gone over to field-grey in 1910 and then covered the helmet as well: the one thing the army did not intend to be seen was itself.
credit: Photograph: Daderot, 2014, of an object in the Braunschweigisches Landesmuseum; via Wikimedia Commons; public domain.
notes: Verified 2026-08-24 against the Commons file record via the MediaWiki API. The museum's date range is 1914–1916 and the caption says so rather than claiming August 1914. The photographer's record notes that photography was unrestricted in the museum.
